verses.text: How the gold has lost its shine! How the pure gold has changed! The sacred stones lie scattered at the corner of every street.
The precious people of Zion were once worth their weight in fine gold. Now they are treated like clay pots made by a potter's hands.
Even jackals nurse their young, but my people have become cruel, like ostriches in the desert.
The nursing baby's tongue sticks to the roof of its mouth from thirst. Children beg for bread, but no one gives them any.
Those who once ate fine food now starve in the streets. Those who were raised wearing royal purple now lie on garbage heaps.
The punishment of my people is greater than the punishment of Sodom, which was destroyed in a moment without anyone lifting a hand against it.
Her princes were brighter than snow and whiter than milk. Their bodies were more glowing than rubies, their appearance like sapphire.
But now they are blacker than soot. No one recognizes them in the streets. Their skin has shriveled on their bones. It has become as dry as wood.
Those killed by the sword are better off than those who die of hunger. The hungry waste away, struck down by the lack of food from the fields.
With their own hands, loving mothers have cooked their own children. Their children became their food when my people were destroyed.
The LORD has unleashed all his anger. He has poured out his fierce anger. He has lit a fire in Zion that burned down its foundations.
The kings of the earth did not believe, nor did anyone in the world, that enemies and foes could enter the gates of Jerusalem.
But it happened because of the sins of her prophets and the wrongs of her priests, who spilled the blood of innocent people inside the city.
Now they wander through the streets like blind men. They are so stained with blood that no one dares to touch their clothes.
People shout at them, "Go away! You are unclean! Go away! Go away! Do not touch us!" So they ran away and wandered. Among the nations people said, "They cannot stay here any longer."
The LORD himself has scattered them. He no longer watches over them. No one respects the priests or shows kindness to the elders.
Our eyes are worn out from looking for help that never came. From our watchtowers we watched for a nation that could not save us.
Our enemies tracked our steps, so we could not walk in our streets. Our end was near. Our days were over. Our end had come.
Those who chased us were faster than eagles in the sky. They hunted us on the mountains and set ambushes for us in the desert.
The LORD's anointed king, the very breath of our life, was caught in their traps. We had thought that under his protection we would live among the nations.
Celebrate and be glad, daughter of Edom, you who live in the land of Uz. But the cup of punishment will come to you too. You will get drunk and strip yourself naked.
Your punishment is complete, daughter of Zion. He will not keep you in exile any longer. But he will punish your sin, daughter of Edom. He will expose your sins.
